title: How Dorothy Saved the Scarecrow, part 5
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “I’m not feeling well,” said the Scarecrow, with a smile, “for it is very tedious being perched up here night and day to scare away crows.”
“No, for this pole is stuck up my back. If you will please take away the pole I shall be greatly obliged to you.”
Dorothy reached up both arms and lifted the figure off the pole, for, being stuffed with straw, it was quite light.
“Thank you very much,” said the Scarecrow, when he had been set down on the ground. “I feel like a new man.”
Dorothy was puzzled at this, for it sounded queer to hear a stuffed man speak, and to see him bow and walk along beside her.
“Who are you?” asked the Scarecrow when he had stretched himself and yawned. “And where are you going?”
“My name is Dorothy,” said the girl, “and I am going to the Emerald City, to ask the Great Oz to send me back to Kansas.”
“Where is the Emerald City?” he inquired. “And who is Oz?”
“Why, don’t you know?” she returned, in surprise.
“No, indeed. I don’t know anything. You see, I am stuffed, so I have no brains at all,” he answered sadly.
“Oh,” said Dorothy, “I’m awfully sorry for you.”
“Do you think,” he asked, “if I go to the Emerald City with you, that Oz would give me some brains?”
“I cannot tell,” she returned, “but you may come with me, if you like. If Oz will not give you any brains you will be no worse off than you are now.”

“That is true,” said the Scarecrow. “You see,” he continued confidentially, “I don’t mind my legs and arms and body being stuffed, because I cannot get hurt. If anyone treads on my toes or sticks a pin into me, it doesn’t matter, for I can’t feel it. But I do not want people to call me a fool, and if my head stays stuffed with straw instead of with brains, as yours is, how am I ever to know anything?”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Scarecrow say he is not feeling well?
options: It is tedious being perched up to scare crows
The pole in his back has torn his coat
The birds have pulled out half his straw
The sun has faded his painted face

questions.prompt: Per the passage, why could the Scarecrow not get down himself?
options: The pole was stuck up his back
His legs were tied to the frame
He was afraid of falling into the corn
He had never learned how to walk

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why was the Scarecrow easy for Dorothy to lift?
options: He was stuffed with straw and quite light
He helped by pulling himself upward
The pole was already loose in the ground
She stood on the fence to reach him

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what does the Scarecrow say he wants from Oz?
options: Some brains
A heart
Courage
A ride to Kansas

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Scarecrow say when set down on the ground?
options: That he feels like a new man
That he would rather go back up
That he cannot feel his own feet
That the straw has shifted about

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Scarecrow not mind his body being stuffed?
options: Nothing can hurt him, however he is treated
Straw is lighter than flesh to carry about
It keeps him from feeling the cold at night
It makes him tall enough to see the road

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Scarecrow fear most about having no brains?
options: That people will call him a fool
That he will forget the way to the city
That the crows will stop being afraid
That Dorothy will not want his company

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what reason does Dorothy give for letting him come along?
options: If Oz refuses, he will be no worse off than now
He knows the road to the Emerald City well
He can carry her basket the whole way
The Witch of the North told her to take him

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does the Scarecrow mean by tedious?
options: Wearisome and dull
Frightening and sudden
Painful to the body
Difficult to explain

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A rescue that gains Dorothy a companion with a wish of his own
A rescue that Dorothy quickly comes to regret
An argument about whether the Scarecrow can think
A lesson in how scarecrows are made in the East

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Scarecrow do after being set on his feet?
options: Stretched himself and yawned
Ran a little way down the road
Sat down beside the fence to rest
Climbed back up onto his pole

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what does the Scarecrow say he knows?
options: Nothing at all
Only the way to the city
Everything the crows have told him
As much as any Munchkin farmer

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Dorothy say she will ask Oz to do for her?
options: Send her back to Kansas
Give her a pair of new shoes
Make her the ruler of the Munchkins
Carry her over the great desert

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what puzzles Dorothy about her new companion?
options: A stuffed man speaks, bows, and walks beside her
He knows her name without being told it
He refuses to say who made him or when
He can lift the basket without growing tired

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Scarecrow not know at the start of the conversation?
options: Where the Emerald City is, or who Oz is
That he is stuffed with straw rather than brains
That Dorothy has come from another country
How long he has been standing on the pole

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does speaking confidentially mean?
options: Telling her something as a private matter
Speaking loudly so that all could hear
Speaking with great certainty of himself
Explaining something over and over

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A stuffed man is freed from his pole and joins the journey
A stuffed man refuses to leave the field he guards
A girl teaches a scarecrow how to walk and talk
A scarecrow warns a girl about the road to the city
